title: Thorn and Ember
premise: Freya Almeida, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics she carves, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things. When a dying courier presses a map into her hands, she discovers it charts the thirteenth moon-turn of King Aldric's reign — the night the thing wearing his crown will finish binding itself to his body. Hunted by the guild she served and guided by the map's dead cartographer, Freya must choose between loyalty to the mentor who raised her and the truth the bones keep whispering: that her own carving hands helped make the crown. In the end, Freya unbinds the king by taking the binding into herself, trading her gift for silence, while the freed king owes a debt to a woman who can no longer hear him say so.
about_author: P. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild ledgers in northern port cities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people whose trades are also their curses.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Freya Almeida balances the Vellum Guild's accounts, carving bone tokens that hum with the voices of the dead sellers. Her mentor, Guildmaster Corvane, praises her discretion. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; she trusts the ledger more than any living person.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Loading Dock
chapters.summary: A bleeding courier staggers into the guild's night dock and presses a rolled map into Freya's hands, whispering 'thirteen turns' before dying. The map's ink moves, and its dead cartographer speaks through Freya's carving knife. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant responsibility as the first voice in years that isn't dead demands something of her.

chapters.title: What Corvane Doesn't Ask
chapters.summary: Freya hides the map, but Corvane notices her distraction and gently probes — too gently. She realizes he already knows what the courier carried. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the first crack in her loyalty; love for her mentor curdles into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Confession
chapters.summary: Through the knife, the dead cartographer Maren explains: the crown on King Aldric's head is a binding vessel, and Freya's own master-carver mother helped forge it. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity — her inheritance is the crime.

chapters.title: Flight from the Vellum Guild
chapters.summary: Guild enforcers come for the map. Freya burns her ledgers as cover and flees through the salt-fog docks with the map and her knife, pursued by her former colleagues. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: grief for the only home she knew, hardened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Road Turns Thrice
chapters.summary: On the north road, Freya meets Tam Vess, a disgraced royal guard deserting his post, who recognizes the map's seal. They distrust each other but travel together when guild hunters attack. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's wounds.

chapters.title: Bone and Ash Village
chapters.summary: They shelter in a village where everyone wears carved bone charms — all silent. Freya realizes someone has been severing the dead from their voices across the region. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: horror at a stolen sacrament; the scale of the enemy becomes real.

chapters.title: The Silencer
chapters.summary: The village's silencer is revealed: Sister Ondine, a guild-trained carver and Corvane's other protégé, who believes silencing the dead brings peace. She lets them live with a warning. POV: Ondine. Emotional beat: chilling conviction — the antagonist believes she is merciful.

chapters.title: What the King Remembers
chapters.summary: In the capital, King Aldric wakes nightly unable to account for hours of his reign. His queen watches him with fear she mistakes for love. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: dread of self-erasure; a man losing the argument with his own reflection.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Countdown
chapters.summary: Maren's map reveals the mechanics: each moon-turn strengthens the crown-thing's hold; on the thirteenth, the binding completes and the king is gone forever. Four turns remain. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: urgency compresses the journey; Freya and Tam grow closer over shared maps and shared lies.

chapters.title: The Queen's Summons
chapters.summary: Queen Isolde intercepts them, not to stop them but to beg their help — she has read her husband's sleep-talk and knows something wears him. POV: Isolde. Emotional beat: love against duty inverted; duty to love over crown.

chapters.title: Corvane's Version
chapters.summary: Corvane captures Freya and offers truth: the guild made the crown to stabilize a kingdom on the edge of civil war, sacrificing one man for thousands. He asks her to help perfect it instead of breaking it. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the seduction of the reasonable argument; loyalty's last stand.

chapters.title: Tam's Desertion, Retold
chapters.summary: Imprisoned with Tam, Freya learns why he fled the palace: he saw the king's eyes change and reported it, and was ordered silenced. His loyalty broke first. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: mutual honesty as armor; love admitted quietly between cell walls.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Bone Gallery
chapters.summary: Freya uses her carving gift to wake the dead stored in the palace ossuary, causing chaos that frees them both. The dead speak her name like a key. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: her curse becomes her power fully claimed.

chapters.title: Ondine's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ondine corners Freya with an offer: help silence the crown-thing permanently — and every dead voice everywhere — or die. Freya refuses, and they duel among the ossuary shelves. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: Freya chooses a world with grief in it over a world with none.

chapters.title: The Mother's Hands
chapters.summary: Maren leads Freya to her long-dead mother's workshop, where the original crown-mold survives. Carving marks match Freya's own hand exactly — her mother trained her unknowingly for maintenance. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: identity shattered and rebuilt; she was made as a tool, and chooses otherwise.

chapters.title: One Turn Remaining
chapters.summary: With one moon-turn left, the group infiltrates the palace during the Night of Bells. Corvane, expecting them, has moved the binding ritual to the throne room. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: calm before catastrophe; Tam accepts he may not survive his second act of conscience.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: In the throne room, the crown-thing manifests through Aldric, wearing his memories like borrowed clothes. It offers Freya her mother back, reconstructed from the dead it holds. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: temptation at its cruelest; love weaponized.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Freya begins the counter-carving on the crown itself as Tam and Isolde hold off Corvane's enforcers. The crown-thing floods her with every dead voice at once. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: agony transfigured into purpose; she listens when listening would destroy her.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: To complete the unbinding, Freya takes the binding into her own bones, shattering the crown and her gift together. The king wakes; Corvane falls; Ondine walks away, unconvinced. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: triumph braided with loss — she saves the king and goes deaf to the dead forever.

chapters.title: A Debt Owed
chapters.summary: Aldric, restored, seeks out Freya to thank her, but she cannot hear his gratitude and he cannot repay what she gave. He abolishes the guild's trade in impossible things instead. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: the awkward grace of debts that cannot be paid, only honored.

chapters.title: Ember, Unheard
chapters.summary: Months later, Freya carves plain bone charms in a coastal village, silent at last, with Tam mending nets beside her. One finished charm hums, faintly — once. She smiles and does not answer it. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: peace chosen, not granted; a door left ajar.
